title: Emergent medium-range order in amorphous silicon
authors: Zhen Zhang, Stephen R. Elliott, Yujie Wang, Walter Kob
abstract: Medium-range order (MRO) is an important feature of amorphous materials, but its nature in terms of atomic arrangement has remained elusive. Here, using large-scale machine-learning-driven atomistic simulations of amorphous silicon, we probe the MRO of this archetypal network glass. By characterizing the structure in three dimensions, we reveal that the symmetry of the atomic arrangement around a central atom shows a crossover as a function of distance. At short distances, the structure is determined by local bonding constraints, which evolve from predominantly tetrahedral environments in low-density amorphous silicon to highly coordinated and strongly disordered local environments in very-high-density amorphous silicon. At larger distances, however, distinct cubic- and octahedral-symmetry patterns emerge in the three-dimensional atomic-density distribution, despite the absence of these symmetries at shorter length scales. We find that this crossover is accompanied by a quasi-periodic spatial organization of the topological rings in the structure. The characteristic spacing between ring centers matches the length scale of the first sharp diffraction peak (FSDP) in the structure factor, establishing a direct connection between this reciprocal-space signature of MRO and its real-space organization. These results demonstrate that the FSDP, the spatial correlation of the rings, and emergent orientational symmetries are not independent manifestations of MRO, but reflect different aspects of a common structural organization. Our findings provide a unified real-space picture of MRO in amorphous silicon and suggest that intermediate-range structural order in network glasses emerges from the interplay between local bonding constraints and extended atomic arrangements driven by efficient packing.
summary: This work uses large-scale simulations on amorphous silicon to map out the structural nature of Medium-Range Order (MRO). It demonstrates that MRO is not a single feature but an emergent property arising from the interplay between local bonding rules and extended, quasi-periodic atomic arrangements. The key finding unifies the structural evidence by showing that the FSDP in diffraction experiments directly corresponds to the characteristic spacing of topological rings in real space.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize the nature of Medium-Range Order (MRO) in amorphous materials, specifically amorphous silicon, and establish a unified understanding of its structural manifestations.
main_result: The paper reveals that MRO is characterized by a crossover in atomic symmetry with distance, linking the reciprocal-space signature (FSDP) to the real-space organization of topological rings and emergent symmetries.
method: The research employs large-scale machine-learning-driven atomistic simulations and analyzes structural properties using four-point correlation functions and topological ring analysis.
model_or_system: The primary system is amorphous silicon (a-Si), an archetypal network glass, studied under varying density conditions (LDA to VHDA) using atomistic simulations.
key_observables: Medium-Range Order (MRO), First Sharp Diffraction Peak (FSDP), topological ring spacing, emergent cubic/octahedral symmetries, and structural correlation length ($\xi$).
important_parameters: Density (low vs. high), Temperature, and characteristic length scales (e.g., FSDP length scale).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that MRO can be understood by examining the interplay between local bonding constraints and extended, quasi-periodic atomic arrangements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the equation of state, structural motifs (LDA vs. VHDA), and the evolution of symmetry and correlation functions with distance.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first characterizing local structure (SRO) and then using higher-order correlation functions to probe MRO, culminating in the direct quantitative link between the FSDP and the real-space ring structure.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter structure, the use of advanced machine learning potentials (GAP) and multi-body correlation functions to characterize emergent order in disordered systems is highly relevant to understanding complex many-body dynamics in open quantum systems.
